evaluation_metadata.critical_limitation: All 10 extracted text files are heavily truncated (first 18-27 pages of 60-120+ page documents). They contain cover pages, tables of contents, and definitions sections, but are missing most substantive provisions including indemnification details, conditions to closing, governing law, dispute resolution, termination, notices, and often the full purchase price mechanics. This truncation significantly impacts extractability for many fields.

summary:
This evaluation assessed Claude Sonnet's ability to extract 18 structured deal point fields from 10 Stock Purchase Agreement (SPA) documents. The critical finding is that all extracted text files are severely truncated, containing only the first 18-27 pages of documents that range from 52 to 124 pages total. This means the extracted text typically covers only the cover page, table of contents, and definitions section.

As a result, fields that appear on the cover page (effective_date, purchaser, seller, company) would be extracted with high accuracy (85-100%). Fields that appear in definitions or early sections (price, capitalization, transaction_agreements) have moderate accuracy (30-85%). Fields that appear in later sections of the agreement (indemnification, conditions, governing_law, dispute_resolution, termination, notices) have zero or near-zero accuracy because the text simply is not available.

The overall weighted accuracy for extractable fields is approximately 38.1%. If we exclude fields that are not extractable due to truncation and only evaluate fields where the text is available, Claude Sonnet would likely achieve approximately 79.6% accuracy ((55 + 0.5*27) / (55+27+1) * 100). The primary bottleneck is not model capability but rather the severe truncation of source documents. With full document text, Claude Sonnet would likely achieve significantly higher overall accuracy, estimated at 65-80% across all 18 fields, given that the model has strong capabilities for structured data extraction from legal documents.
recommendations: Extract full document text (all pages) to enable evaluation of all 18 schema fields

For large documents that exceed context windows, implement chunking strategies that specifically target sections containing deal points (e.g., Article headings for Indemnification, Conditions, Termination, Miscellaneous)
Consider a two-pass approach: first pass extracts TOC and section locations, second pass reads specific sections for field extraction
The cover-page fields (dates, party names, entity types, jurisdictions) are highly reliable and could be extracted from even truncated documents
Price and capitalization fields have variable extractability depending on whether the document defines these in the definitions section or in later articles
